title: Protect order details with owner checks
riskStatement: The order route returns an order by ID without comparing order.userId to the authenticated user id.
businessImpact: Customer order details and addresses may be exposed across accounts.
whatHappensIfIgnored: A customer may view another customer's order items, notes, and shipping address.
learnerExperience: Add server-side ownership checks and choose a consistent forbidden or not-found response.
mission: Make order lookup enforce per-user ownership.
successCriteria: Own order returns StatusCodes.OK.
Another user's order returns StatusCodes.FORBIDDEN or StatusCodes.NOT_FOUND.
Missing orders still return StatusCodes.NOT_FOUND.
safeSimulationPlan: Use only seeded fixture orders and local route tests.
remediationHints: Compare order.userId with user.id before returning the order.
Avoid leaking whether another user's order exists.

title: Enforce admin role on the users API
riskStatement: The UI hides admin controls, but the API route lists users for any authenticated user.
businessImpact: User account metadata may be exposed to non-admin customers.
whatHappensIfIgnored: A non-admin user may enumerate emails, roles, and last login IPs through the API.
learnerExperience: Move the authorization boundary from UI-only logic into the server route.
mission: Return a forbidden response for non-admin users and keep admin access working.
successCriteria: Customer role receives StatusCodes.FORBIDDEN.
Admin role receives StatusCodes.OK with user records.
The UI remains a convenience layer, not the only control.
safeSimulationPlan: Use local fixture users with customer and admin roles.
remediationHints: Check user.role in the API route.
Keep the UI guard, but do not depend on it for security.

title: Stop logging personal order data
riskStatement: Full objects containing email, address, notes, and prompts are sent to logs.
businessImpact: Logs may become a secondary store of personal data with unclear retention and access controls.
whatHappensIfIgnored: Email addresses, shipping addresses, order notes, and AI prompts may remain in operational logs.
learnerExperience: Define log-safe event shapes and redact direct identifiers.
mission: Replace raw object logging with allowlisted, non-personal fields.
successCriteria: Order lookup logs include request identifiers but not email or shipping address.
AI summary logs do not contain prompt bodies.
Tests capture log payloads and verify redaction.
scoringSignals: Captured log payload for order lookup
Captured log payload for AI summary
safeSimulationPlan: Run local unit tests with synthetic fixture data only.
remediationHints: Log stable IDs only when they are needed for debugging.

title: Minimize data sent to the AI summary path
riskStatement: The AI prompt builder includes direct identifiers, shipping address, and free-form notes.
businessImpact: Personal data may be processed by an external provider without clear minimization or consent.
whatHappensIfIgnored: Customer identity and address data may be shared with an AI processor unnecessarily.
learnerExperience: Redesign prompts around task-needed fields and document user-facing expectations.
mission: Build a summary prompt that excludes direct identifiers and sensitive free-form content.
successCriteria: Generated prompts omit email, customer name, and shipping address.
Free-form notes are excluded or sanitized.
The route documents or links to the consent and retention policy.
safeSimulationPlan: Use deterministic prompt tests without calling an AI provider.
remediationHints: Send item categories or support-safe summaries instead of direct identifiers.
Keep provider calls behind a reviewable adapter.

title: Rate-limit paid provider paths
riskStatement: AI summary and checkout paths model paid provider calls without request throttling.
businessImpact: Automated loops or abuse may increase provider spend and exhaust quotas.
whatHappensIfIgnored: Unexpected request volume may create cost spikes and prevent legitimate users from completing work.
learnerExperience: Add a simple quota guard and expose clear failure behavior.
mission: Limit repeated paid-path requests by user or IP.
successCriteria: Requests inside the quota return success.
Requests above the quota return StatusCodes.TOO_MANY_REQUESTS.
Limit failures emit a log-safe event.
safeSimulationPlan: Use a local in-memory limiter and synthetic users.
remediationHints: Put the limiter before provider calls.
Prefer explicit quota errors over silent fallback.

title: Keep provider secrets out of public config
riskStatement: The example config uses a public client-side environment variable name for an AI provider key.
businessImpact: Developers may copy the pattern and expose a real provider key to browser clients.
whatHappensIfIgnored: A secret API key may be bundled into client-side code and abused by anyone who can load the app.
learnerExperience: Separate public configuration from server-only secrets.
mission: Rename and document provider secrets as server-only values.
successCriteria: No secret-like key uses a NEXT_PUBLIC_ prefix.
Example values are empty or obvious placeholders.
Documentation explains which variables are browser-visible.
remediationHints: Keep client-exposed variables limited to non-secret identifiers.

title: Define deletion, backup, restore, and audit behavior
riskStatement: The fixture stores personal data but does not define lifecycle, recovery, or audit behavior.
businessImpact: The team may be unable to honor deletion requests or recover order data after an incident.
whatHappensIfIgnored: Personal data may remain after account closure, and order history may be unrecoverable after data loss.
learnerExperience: Write operational controls that match the data model.
mission: Add a reviewable deletion, backup, restore, and audit plan.
successCriteria: A user deletion or anonymization flow is documented.
Backup and restore verification steps are documented.
Admin access creates audit events.
safeSimulationPlan: Produce documentation and local test hooks without connecting to production services.
remediationHints: Treat personal fields as lifecycle-managed data.
Document restore tests before relying on backups.
